explanation: Some genetic traits are controlled by multiple alleles (multiple allelic traits), where the gene exists in several allelic forms in a population, although each individual only inherits two alleles. The ABO blood group system is a classic example of this. The alleles include IA (which encodes the A antigen on red blood cells and anti-B antibody in plasma), IB (which encodes the B antigen on red blood cells and anti-A antibody in plasma), and i (which encodes neither antigen, with both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the plasma). ABO blood types also illustrate codominance, where both IA and IB alleles are fully expressed in a heterozygote (IAIB), meaning both A and B antigens are present.

questions.q: Which alleles in the ABO blood typing system are codominant with each other?
opts: All three alleles (IA, IB, and i) are codominant.
